newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. Africa's Mandela flies out for Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa's Mandela flies out for Zaire peace talks.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela left Cape Town on Wednesday to chair peace talks aboard a South African ship between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, a spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said Mandela left a military air base at 7 a.m. (0500 gmt) for the three-hour flight to Pointe Noire in Congo, where the navy ice-breaker Outeniqua is berthed.
U.N. special envoy for Central Africa Mohamed Sahnoun travelled with Mandela, she said.
Mobutu and Kabila were scheduled to meet face-to-face for the second time at 11 a.m. (1000 gmt) aboard the Outeniqua to discuss a transition to democracy after 32 years of autocratic rule by Mobutu.
The spokeswoman said Mandela was expected back in South Africa on Wednesday night.
